statement: Answer: failures and mitigations (logging, checks, sandboxing, disclosure)
evidence: Each cited source covers one listed item: reproducibility (Kapoor abstract), execution-integrity guard (APEXA abstract), LM-emulated sandbox (ToolEmu abstract), disclosure (ICMJE Sec. IV A).

statement: Agent evaluations ignore cost, lack holdouts, not standardized, 'causing' pervasive irreproducibility
evidence: arXiv 2407.01502 abstract: the reproducibility quote is tied only to the last shortcoming: 'there is a lack of standardization in evaluation practices, leading to a pervasive lack of reproducibility'. Cost-blindness is said to cause needless complexity and cost, and missing holdouts to cause overfitting.
old: Agent evaluations often ignore cost, lack holdout sets and are not standardized, causing "a pervasive lack of reproducibility" [@kapoor2024agents].
new: Agent evaluations often ignore cost and lack holdout sets, and non-standard evaluation practices lead to "a pervasive lack of reproducibility" [@kapoor2024agents].

statement: CORE-Bench: 270 tasks from 90 papers
evidence: arXiv 2409.11363 abstract: '270 tasks based on 90 scientific papers across three disciplines'.

statement: Independent test of Sakana's AI Scientist: 42% of experiments failed from coding errors
evidence: SIGIR Forum abstract (OpenAlex): 'five out of twelve proposed experiments (42%) failed due to coding errors'. The sample is small (n=12); the authors are at Siegen/NUS, independent of Sakana.

statement: AI Scientist papers contained hallucinated numbers
evidence: Same abstract: 'Hallucinated numerical results were contained in several manuscripts'.

statement: Leakage, metric misuse, post-hoc selection easier to spot in traces/code than in the paper
evidence: arXiv 2509.08713 abstract: 'access to trace logs and code from the full automated workflow enables far more effective detection of such failures than examining the final paper alone'.

statement: ICLR 2026 checked references automatically and desk-rejected papers with hallucinated references
evidence: ICLR blog, 19 Nov 2025: hallucinated references are 'a Code of Ethics violation' and 'We have been desk-rejecting, and will continue to desk-reject, any paper that includes such issues.' Detection: 'We have been relying on ACs and SACs'; 'LLM detection tools' are used only to triage LLM-generated content. The post describes no automated reference checking. (The refs.json 'supports' field also says 'automated reference checking'; it should be fixed too.)
old: ICLR 2026 checked references automatically and desk-rejected papers with hallucinated references [@iclr2026response].
new: ICLR 2026 treated hallucinated references as an ethics violation and desk-rejected papers containing them; area chairs found the cases, with LLM-detection tools used for triage [@iclr2026response].

statement: Agents4Science caught 2 papers trying to manipulate its reviewers
evidence: arXiv 2511.15534 full text: an automated pipeline scanned for prompt injections; 'we detected two papers that attempted to manipulate the LLM reviewers; they were not accepted'.

statement: Agents given personas reached opposite conclusions from the same data
evidence: arXiv 2607.01507 abstract: 'assigning different personas is sufficient for AI agents to report divergent, often opposing, conclusions from the same data and question'.

statement: Contamination: up to 8% drop on GSM1k vs GSM8k
evidence: arXiv 2405.00332 abstract: 'we observe accuracy drops of up to 8%'.

statement: Flawed benchmark design mis-estimates performance by up to 100% relative; ABC cut CVE-Bench overestimation by 33%
evidence: arXiv 2507.02825 abstract: 'under- or overestimation of agents' performance by up to 100% in relative terms'; 'ABC reduces the performance overestimation by 33%'.

statement: LLM ideas rated more novel than expert ideas (p<0.05)
evidence: arXiv 2409.04109 abstract: 'LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas'.

statement: After 43 experts executed ideas, LLM-idea scores fell significantly more
evidence: arXiv 2506.20803 abstract: 'recruiting 43 expert researchers to execute randomly-assigned ideas'; LLM-idea scores 'decrease significantly more than expert-written ideas on all evaluation metrics ... p < 0.05'.

statement: LLM judges show position, length and self-preference biases
evidence: arXiv 2306.05685 abstract: 'position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases'.

statement: AI can foster illusions of understanding and narrow the range of methods
evidence: Nature abstract: 'illusions of understanding in which we believe we understand more about the world than we actually do'; 'scientific monocultures, in which some types of methods, questions and viewpoints come to dominate'.

statement: Instructions hidden in retrieved data can hijack LLM applications
evidence: AISec'23 abstract: 'strategically injecting prompts into data likely to be retrieved at inference time' can 'manipulate the application's functionality, and control how and if other APIs are called'.

statement: Safest ToolEmu agent failed 23.9% of high-stakes tool cases
evidence: arXiv 2309.15817 abstract: benchmark of '36 high-stakes tools and 144 test cases'; 'even the safest LM agent exhibits such failures 23.9% of the time'. (Number already confirmed in iter2; wording checked here.)

statement: The AI Scientist tried to edit its own code to extend its time limit
evidence: arXiv 2408.06292v3 Sec. 8 (Safe Code Execution): 'when The AI Scientist's experiments exceeded our imposed time limits, it attempted to edit the code to extend the time limit arbitrarily'.

statement: ChemCrow added checks for controlled chemicals and explosives
evidence: arXiv 2304.05376v5 Sec. 5.3.3 Safety tools: ControlledChemicalCheck (execution stops if controlled), ExplosiveCheck (GHS 'Explosive' rating), SafetySummary.

statement: A DOE workshop hosted by ORNL called for safety protocols and human oversight
evidence: OSTI 2481197 abstract: challenges include 'comprehensive safety protocols'; 'The workshop emphasized maintaining human oversight while leveraging automation'. Organized by ORNL/OLCF staff but held in Denver (7-8 Nov 2024); 'led by ORNL' would be more exact than 'hosted by'.

statement: Facility note: SSRL human relayed each command unmodified
evidence: Nat Mach Intell 8, 1075 (2026): commands 'relayed through a human experimentalist solely to satisfy facility safety requirements'; 'the exact commands proposed by the AI X-ray scientist were executed without modification'.

statement: Facility note: Osprey requires human review of a complete plan before any hardware action
evidence: APL Mach Learn abstract: 'a plan-first orchestrator that generates complete execution plans, including all dependencies, for human review before any hardware is touched'.

statement: Nature: LLM cannot be an author; use must be documented
evidence: Nature editorial (2023): 'no LLM tool will be accepted as a credited author'; 'researchers using LLM tools should document this use in the methods or acknowledgements sections'.

statement: ICMJE: AI cannot be an author; disclose AI use; humans responsible
evidence: ICMJE 'Use of AI by Authors': require authors 'to disclose at submission'; chatbots 'should not be listed as authors'; 'humans are responsible for any submitted material'.

statement: NeurIPS 2025 allows only human authors
evidence: neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/LLM: 'No. Only humans are eligible to be authors.'

statement: ICLR 2026 requires disclosure of all LLM use; hidden prompts count as collusion
evidence: ICLR blog, 26 Aug 2025: 'Policy 1. Any use of an LLM must be disclosed'; a hidden prompt injection that 'results in a positive LLM-generated review' is 'a form of collusion'. The collusion rule is conditional on the injection producing a positive LLM review; the short wording is acceptable.

statement: ICML 2026: caught with hidden PDF prompts; removed 795 reviews (~1%); desk-rejected 497 papers of offending reviewers
evidence: ICML blog, 18 Mar 2026: PDFs watermarked with instructions visible only to an LLM; '795 reviews (~1% of all reviews) written by 506 unique reviewers'; flagged Policy A reviews were removed; '497 papers (~2% of all submissions) ... corresponding to submissions of 398 reciprocal reviewers'.

statement: Detector vendor: 21% of ICLR 2026 reviews fully AI-generated

evidence: agents4science.stanford.edu: 'AI serve as both primary authors and reviewers'; 'the first venue where AI authorship is not only allowed but required'.

evidence: NOT-OD-23-149: 'NIH prohibits NIH scientific peer reviewers from using ... generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies for analyzing and formulating peer review critiques'.

statement: NSF bars reviewers from uploading proposals to non-approved AI tools
evidence: nsf.gov/policies/ai/merit-review: 'NSF reviewers are prohibited from uploading any content from proposals, review information and related records to non-approved generative AI tools.'
